info.name: HeyGen V3 - Background Color Test
info.description: Minimal, standalone test for one specific question: does V3 actually honor the requested background.value color for a photo_avatar-type avatar? On 2026-07-26, the same request against Daniel Mercer (avatar_type=digital_twin, engine=avatar_iv) silently rendered flat gray instead of the requested #00FF00 green (video had a 'Veo' watermark, suggesting that avatar type may render through Google Veo rather than HeyGen's own renderer). Zayne Carter is avatar_type=photo_avatar - a different underlying avatar type, not yet tested. Set HEYGEN_API_KEY before use.

variable.description: Auto-populated by the Submit request's test script

item.name: 1. Submit - Zayne Carter, green bg, avatar_iv

request.description: Zayne Carter (photo_avatar type, not digital_twin/PAOS) with the same #00FF00 green background request that silently came out gray for Daniel Mercer. No motion_prompt included, to keep this test isolated to the background-color question only.

exec: if (id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('video_id', id); console.log('video_id set:', id); }
else { console.log('No video_id in response:', JSON.stringify(json)); }

item.name: 1b. Submit - Zayne Carter, green bg, avatar_v (alternate engine)

request.description: Only run this one if #1 also comes back gray (or another wrong color) - isolates whether it's an avatar_iv-specific issue or affects avatar_v too. Zayne supports avatar_v per the roster capability audit, so motion_prompt is safe to include here.

exec: if (id) { pm.collectionVariables.set('video_id', id); console.log('video_id set:', id); }
else { console.log('No video_id in response:', JSON.stringify(json)); }

request.description: Re-send this every 15-30s until data.status == 'completed'. Then open data.video_url in a browser and look at the background: is it actually solid green (#00FF00), or did it come out some other flat color again? Also check for a 'Veo' watermark in the corner - if present, that avatar/engine combo is likely rendering through Google Veo rather than HeyGen's own pipeline, which may explain why the color param isn't honored.
